anomalies.observed: R59 has a value field of "24k" but its description says "24Ω" and its MPN is "FRC0805J240TSD", a 24Ω part. The SPICE deck also models R59 as 24k.
anomalies.expected: The value should match the part metadata and intended role. A 24k resistor across VOUTP/VOUTN is a plausible bleeder; a 24Ω part would be a heavy load, especially on a PoE-derived rail.

evidence.quote: (comp (ref "R59") (value "24k") ... (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS") ... (field (name "MPN") "FRC0805J240TSD"))

anomalies.impact: If the board is assembled with the specified MPN (24Ω), R59 will present a near-short across VOUTP/VOUTN, causing excessive current and possible damage. If the 24k value is intended, the BOM part is wrong and the board will not match the schematic.

anomalies.observed: The VP/VCC pins (pin 5) of U33 and U50 are marked as no-connect/unconnected in the netlist.
anomalies.expected: For TPD4E1U06 / AOZ8904CIL ESD protection arrays, the VP pin must be connected to the positive supply rail of the protected interface (e.g., +3V3 or +5V) to clamp positive ESD transients.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet ESD protection is incomplete; positive ESD events may not be properly clamped, increasing the risk of damage to the Ethernet interface.

parsed.summary: The design files contain two anomalies: R59 has a value of 24k while its description and MPN specify a 24Ω part, and the VP/VCC pins of the Ethernet ESD protection devices U33 and U50 are left unconnected. Both are deviations from sound design practice and would affect board reliability or assembly.
